title: Safe De-escalation of Chemotherapy for Stage 1 Breast Cancer
official: Safe De-escalation of Chemotherapy for Stage 1 Breast Cancer
summary:
The SAFE-DE study investigates whether circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing can guide adjuvant treatment decisions in patients with stage I breast cancer, identifying those who may be able to avoid chemotherapy after surgery. The study includes patients with stage I HER2-positive breast cancer and patients with stage I triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) with high levels of tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs). The Signatera personalised ctDNA assay is used to detect molecular residual disease (MRD), which may indicate that cancer remains in the body after surgery.

SAFE-DE comprises two parts. Part A, which is closed to recruitment, investigated the incidence of post-operative ctDNA detection and its association with subsequent outcomes, including the potential prognostic significance of pre-operative ctDNA. Part B builds on this work by prospectively evaluating whether ctDNA-guided treatment and surveillance can reduce the use of adjuvant chemotherapy while maintaining favourable cancer outcomes.

Patients may be enrolled before surgery to facilitate pre-operative sampling and timely post-operative testing. Blood samples will be collected after surgery, including at 2 and 4 weeks. The results of the 2- and 4-week post-operative ctDNA tests will be shared with patients and their treating clinicians to inform treatment decisions in accordance with the study protocol and individual clinical circumstances. Pre-operative ctDNA results will be investigated as an exploratory measure and will not be disclosed for treatment decisions.

Patients with detectable ctDNA after surgery will be recommended standard adjuvant systemic treatment. Patients with no detectable ctDNA at both 2 and 4 weeks after surgery will be recommended not to receive adjuvant chemotherapy and will instead enter a ctDNA surveillance programme. If ctDNA becomes detectable during surveillance, patients will then be offered standard adjuvant treatment.

The primary purpose of Part B is to assess whether patients with undetectable ctDNA following surgery can remain free from distant recurrence without adjuvant chemotherapy. Additional outcomes include recurrence and survival, adjuvant treatment use, ctDNA detection during surveillance, quality of life and the cost-effectiveness of ctDNA-guided treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age 18 years or older
2. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0,1 or 2
3. Have an estimated life expectancy of at least 5 years
4. Histologically confirmed breast cancer that is either:

   (A) HER2-positive as defined by 2023 ASCO-CAP guidelines determined by local testing\* or (B) Triple negative defined as ER negative (ER staining in \<1% tumour cells or ER Allred score \<3/8) and PR negative (PR staining in \<10% tumour cells or PR Allred score \<6/8) and HER2-negative by 2023 ASCO-CAP guidelines determined by local testing. Patients without PR testing results may enrol on the basis of ER and HER2 results.

   \* Note: Patients negative for ER and PR may enrol whilst awaiting HER2 testing results
5. Pathological stage 1 cancer as below: \*\*

   EITHER
   1. HER2-positive invasive tumour size 5-20mm OR
   2. TNBC invasive tumour size 5-20mm, with high TILs (stromal tumour infiltration lymphocytes \>30%) determined by central testing

   AND (c) Node negative (isolated tumour cells are allowed)

   \*\*Patients may be enrolled pre-operatively with clinical stage 1 cancer with primary tumour size on imaging 5-20mm and a normal axilla ultrasound or a biopsy negative axilla. Patients enrolled before surgery will only continue in study after surgery when confirmed pathological stage 1
6. Planned for and fit enough to receive standard post-operative chemotherapy, with HER2 targeting as appropriate, in the opinion of the investigator
7. Able and willing to provide written informed consent or remote consent
8. Negative serum pregnancy test at screening (females of childbearing potential). Patients able to have children are advised to use a method of contraception, or abstinence, throughout the ctDNA surveillance period
9. Willing and able to comply with scheduled visits, laboratory tests and other procedures
10. Available tissue from breast surgery or diagnostic core (preference to diagnostic core for rapidity of tissue sequencing).

Exclusion criteria:

1. Prior treatment for the current breast cancer, other than surgery if recruited post-operatively
2. Multifocal invasive cancer
3. Micrometastasis or macrometastasis in axillary lymph nodes
4. pT1a invasive tumour size \<5mm
5. Distant metastatic disease on imaging performed as part of standard of care
6. Planned participation in an alternative treatment trial
7. Diagnosis of alternative cancer within the last 5 years except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, or carcinoma in situ of the breast or cervix
8. Known HIV or AIDS-related illness
9. Known positive HBV or HCV test indicating acute or chronic infection
